claims.statement: NIS2 creates risk-management and reporting duties across 18 critical sectors and explicitly covers supply-chain security, vulnerability handling, and incident response.
ENISA has recommended common risk-assessment language and lightweight underwriting processes for SME cyber insurance.
ENISA reports that SMEs can be targeted directly and used as routes into larger organizations' supply chains.

contrary_evidence: NIS2 generally focuses on medium and large entities in covered sectors, so many small customers are not directly compelled.
The Commission proposed 2026 simplifications that may reduce compliance burden, and ENISA's insurance-process recommendations do not prove insurer adoption of this product.

economics.acquisition_route: Broker and MSP bundles rather than direct one-by-one SME sales
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 1000 SMEs averaging 600 PLN monthly could reach 7.2m PLN recurring revenue; at 25% operating margin and 75% ownership, a profit-based valuation could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 6
economics.founder_time: 3 hours/day for integrations and analytics, with cyber audit and insurance expertise contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 70-85% after integrations, scanning, support, security assurance, and broker revenue share
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 80 SMEs averaging 500 PLN monthly could repay the pilot in 12-18 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 300-1000 PLN per SME monthly plus channel setup or per-passport fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Continuous evidence updates and annual policy or supplier reviews create recurring use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Accepted evidence schema, control-change history, claims or incident feedback, and embedded renewal distribution
fingerprint.customer: European SMEs, cyber insurers, brokers, MSPs, and large buyers assessing suppliers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: One insurance broker or MSP channel, then buyer supplier-assurance programmes
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Read-only integrations, control evidence, remediation queue, signed passport, and renewal export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: SME pays monthly; broker, insurer, or buyer may pay per completed evidence pack or channel seat
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An SME seeks a policy quote or renewal, enters a supply chain, or must show current cyber controls

founder_fit: Uses data integration, anomaly detection, and automation
Low-capital software pilot is compatible with employment
Can build evidence gradually without acting as an insurer
risks: A passport can create false assurance and liability after an incident
Read-only integrations still expose sensitive security metadata
Insurers may keep proprietary questionnaires and decline a shared format

structure.control_point: The evidence format and live control feed accepted at policy renewal or supplier approval
structure.critical_dependency: A broker, insurer, or major buyer must accept the passport and return outcome data sufficient to calibrate it

thesis: Continuously collect lightweight, machine-verifiable cyber controls from an SME's existing tools and issue a time-stamped evidence passport for insurance quotation, renewal, and larger-customer procurement. Distribution begins through a broker or managed-service provider; the defensible position is the accepted renewal gate and outcome-calibrated evidence schema, not another security checklist.
title: Insurer-Accepted SME Cyber Evidence Passport
uncertainties: Which insurer or broker will accept the evidence as a decision input
Access to loss or incident outcomes for calibration
Whether SMEs will pay separately when MSP tools already generate reports
